data.title: Dow drops below 50K for the first time in 5 months
data.description:
U.S. equities retreated sharply on Thursday afternoon, pushing the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) below 50,000 for the first time since mid-June and to its lowest level since May 5. 

The blue-chip index fell roughly 2% on the session and now stands -10.3% below its all-time trading high of 54,744, reached back on August 5. 

The decline leaves the Dow more than 5,000 points off that peak, reflecting a sustained pullback from the summer highs.

Moreover, the leg lower on the session was fueled by basically all the components within the Dow, with 29 of the 30 names in the red. The one green spot belonged to Chevron (CVX). 

Spotlighted below are the top 10 worst Dow performers on Thursday: 

  1. Nike (NKE), -5.6%.
  2. UnitedHealth Group (UNH), -5.1%.
  3. Merck & Company (MRK), -4.3%. 
  4. Amazon.com (AMZN), -3.6%.
  5. Salesforce (CRM), -3.4%. 
  6. Visa (V), -3.1%.
  7. Caterpillar (CAT), -3.1%.
  8. Alphabet (GOOGL), -2.7%. 
  9. Johnson & Johnson (JNJ), -2.5%. 
  10. Goldman Sachs Group (GS), -2.4%. 

Dow ETFs: (DIA), (DDM), (UDOW), (DOG), (DXD), and (SDOW).

data.title: It’s a ‘dark period for tech’ as Anthropic debuts IPO – Dan Ives
data.description:
Anthropic's (ANT) public debut marks a watershed moment for the technology sector (XLK) even as broader markets endure what Dan Ives, co-partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., called "a dark period for tech" in an interview with CNBC.

While the AI company's IPO demonstrated strong institutional appetite during its roadshow, the S&P 500 (SP500) has fallen for six consecutive days, and the entire AI stock stack has pulled back sharply.

Ives described the current market environment as "a tale of two cities," with Anthropic's successful offering standing in stark contrast to widespread investor anxiety.

He attributed the tech sector's struggles to concerns surrounding Nvidia (NVDA) and China, as well as broader uncertainty that has sent the VIX Volatility Index to 28—its highest level since March.

Despite the turbulence, Ives characterized the downturn as "a panic moment" rather than a fundamental shift in the technology landscape.

"We're less than 15% through the build out of the AI revolution," he said, adding that the foundational bull thesis for tech remains intact.

The analyst emphasized that Anthropic's IPO (ANT) could pave the way for OpenAI's (OPENAI) expected public offering in early 2027, underscoring the continued momentum in artificial intelligence development.

He noted that if Anthropic (ANT) succeeds in generating substantial annual revenue over the next five to seven years, the company could see its valuation grow significantly.

Ives pointed to expected capital expenditure growth as a key driver for the sector, projecting $1.3T to $1.5T in AI infrastructure spending next year. Anthropic (ANT), he said, will be "a huge piece of that" alongside other frontier AI models and companies in cybersecurity and software.

Looking ahead, Ives suggested that the current market anxiety will eventually be viewed as a buying opportunity.

"I think we're going to look back in this period, just like April 2025 Liberation Day, and March 2020 during COVID as the opportunity," he said, dismissing comparisons to the 2007 bubble given current valuations and growth fundamentals.

data.title: Maximus forecasts $700M-$800M fiscal 2027 free cash flow while integrating Agile Defense
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Maximus (MMS) Q4 fiscal 2026

Management View

  • "Fiscal year 2026 reflected the benefits of disciplined operations, technology-enabled productivity enhancement and thoughtful capital allocation" (President, CEO & Director Bruce L. Caswell). "Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 14.2% this fiscal year compared to 12.9% in fiscal year 2025" and "adjusted earnings per share increased to $8.24 from $7.36 a year ago" (President, CEO & Director Caswell).

  • "I'm pleased to announce that the acquisition has closed and the integration is underway" (President, CEO & Director Caswell). "We expect that momentum to support double-digit organic growth for Agile in calendar year 2027 on revenue of roughly $450 million" and "with Agile, Defense and National Security represents close to 10% of the total company's revenue" (President, CEO & Director Caswell).

  • "During fiscal year 2026, our recompete win rate was approximately 89%" (President, CEO & Director Caswell). "In the fourth quarter, Maximus rewon a significant health care-related state contract representing more than $800 million of total contract value over 10 years" and "we also recently secured 2 additional important state contract renewals totaling $528 million" (President, CEO & Director Caswell).

  • "Revenue was within our guidance range, and adjusted earnings per share finished $0.04 above the top end of the range" (CFO & Treasurer David Mutryn). "While certain collections slipped beyond September 30 and impacted reported free cash flow in fiscal year 2026, we have subsequently collected most of the anticipated balance and those receipts support our outsized free cash flow guidance for fiscal year 2027" (CFO Mutryn).

Outlook

  • "We expect fiscal year 2027 revenue to range between $5.45 billion and $5.65 billion" (CFO Mutryn). "Our fiscal year 2027 adjusted earnings per share guidance is $7.50 to $8 per share" (CFO Mutryn).

  • "On the VA MDE program, we haven't included any incentive contribution or similar benefit across all 4 quarters of fiscal year 2027" (CFO Mutryn). "This compares to 3 quarters in fiscal year 2026 which contained incentives worth approximately $25 million of revenue and profit per quarter" (CFO Mutryn).

  • "We currently expect to repurchase approximately $200 million worth of shares during fiscal year 2027" (CFO Mutryn). "Allowing for the $200 million of planned share repurchases, we would expect to finish fiscal year 2027 at or below a 2x net debt ratio" (CFO Mutryn).

  • Change from the prior quarter’s call: management moved from Q3’s discussion of a "range of scenarios" for VA MDE incentives and an “early look” at FY2027 to formal FY2027 guidance in Q4, explicitly assuming "no incentive contribution" for all quarters of FY2027 (CFO Mutryn; CFO Mutryn in Q3).

Financial Results

  • "For the full fiscal year 2026, Maximus reported revenue of $5.23 billion" (CFO Mutryn). "Adjusted EBITDA margin was 14.2% and adjusted diluted earnings per share were $8.24" (CFO Mutryn).

  • "U.S. Federal Services revenue was $3.0 billion" and "the operating income margin for U.S. Federal Services was 18.1%" (CFO Mutryn). "The fourth quarter results reflected the contract modification, but also benefited from otherwise strong financial performance on this program as well as higher volumes on a separate clinical program in the segment both of which we anticipate moderating in fiscal year 2027" (CFO Mutryn).

  • "Fiscal year 2026 revenue was $1.68 billion" for U.S. Services and "the U.S. Services operating income margin was 9.1%" (CFO Mutryn). "Fiscal year 2026 included a $6.9 million noncash impairment charge" (CFO Mutryn).

  • "Free cash flow was $69 million" in fiscal 2026 (CFO Mutryn). "Subsequent to September 30 and through November 13, we collected over $330 million from the one customer that we have mentioned in prior quarters" (CFO Mutryn).

Q&A

  • Charles Strauzer, CJS Securities, Inc.: Asked about differences between the draft and final VA MDE RFP; President, CEO & Director Caswell answered, "the final RFP really stayed largely aligned with the draft RFP" and said "the due date is December 17" with "the base period of performance ... scheduled to start July 1, 2027," adding "The new contract doesn't include the same incentive, disincentive structure from the old contract" (President, CEO & Director Caswell).

  • Charles Strauzer, CJS Securities, Inc.: Asked for organic growth framing with Agile included; CFO Mutryn said, "Our implied organic growth at the midpoint of the 2027 revenue guidance is about 1%" and "If you exclude the impact of the VA incentives earned in fiscal year '26, organic growth on that adjusted basis would be a little over 2%" (CFO Mutryn).

  • Brian Gesuale, Raymond James: Asked for magnitude of OBBBA catalysts; CFO Mutryn said, "our guide for the U.S. Services segment of growing mid-single digit from '26 to '27, that's really the primary driver of that growth" (CFO Mutryn).

  • Brian Gesuale, Raymond James: Asked to confirm the MDE incentive revenue/profit headwind embedded in guidance; CFO Mutryn replied, "That's right" (CFO Mutryn).

  • Brian Gesuale, Raymond James: Asked about the role of Outside the U.S.; President, CEO & Director Caswell said, "we are operating right now in a period of some uncertainty for that business" and added, "we think a 1% to 3% operating income margin in over this next year is probably more realistic" (President, CEO & Director Caswell).

  • Brian Gesuale, Raymond James: Asked what share of revenue defense/national security represents with Agile; CFO Mutryn said, "that puts it at about 10% of total company revenue" (CFO Mutryn).

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts: Slightly negative to neutral, with repeated clarification requests on guidance building blocks and organic growth math, including "How much revenue contribution you expect" and whether to model "a negative $75 million kind of annual revenue headwind" (Brian Gesuale, Raymond James; Brian Gesuale, Raymond James).

  • Management: Slightly positive in prepared remarks and generally confident in Q&A, using affirmative language such as "we strongly believe" regarding Agile and "there really were no surprises" on the VA RFP, while also flagging uncertainty in specific areas like Outside the U.S. as "a period of some uncertainty" (President, CEO & Director Caswell).

  • Versus the prior quarter: the Q4 call’s tone was more definitive on forward assumptions, moving from Q3’s "range of scenarios" on VA incentives to Q4’s explicit FY2027 assumption of "no incentive contribution" across all quarters, while maintaining Q3’s view that procurement delays were "not indicative of weakening demand" (CFO Mutryn; President, CEO & Director Caswell).

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Agile Defense shifted from Q3’s stated interest in acquisitions that "can expand capabilities, customer access and longer-term organic growth opportunities" to Q4’s announcement that "the acquisition has closed," with FY2027 guidance now including a "roughly 10-month contribution" (CFO Mutryn in Q3; President, CEO & Director Caswell; CFO Mutryn).

  • VA MDE evolved from Q3’s disclosure of a "temporary pause" in incentives and a preliminary "Draft Performance Work Statement" to Q4’s details on the formal solicitation, including "a submission due date in mid-December" and a restructured model where "vendors who are performing well ... have the opportunity to take on greater volumes" (President, CEO & Director Caswell).

  • Pipeline messaging changed as management said Q4 pipeline was $44.8 billion and that the quarter-over-quarter decline was "due almost entirely to the VA MDE recompete structure" shifting to a "5-year opportunity" from "the 10-year period previously assumed"; Q3 pipeline was described at $50.4 billion amid "procurement delays" in federal civilian (President, CEO & Director Caswell; President, CEO & Director Caswell in Q3).

Risks and Concerns

  • "We also continue to see procurement timing shifts and delays in certain areas of the federal market with civilian being one of the most highly affected areas" (President, CEO & Director Caswell). "We do not view this as indicative of weakening demand" (President, CEO & Director Caswell).

  • "Within the U.S. Federal Services segment, we aimed for a conservative approach" and "we haven't included any incentive contribution" for VA MDE in FY2027 (CFO Mutryn). Management’s mitigation emphasized portfolio diversification via Agile, saying "U.S. Federal Services will emerge as a stronger, less concentrated segment" (CFO Mutryn).

  • "Cash collection timing remained an important theme" and FY2026 free cash flow reflected that "certain collections slipped beyond September 30" (CFO Mutryn). The mitigation cited was subsequent receipts, including "we collected over $330 million" after year-end (CFO Mutryn).

Final Takeaway

Management said fiscal 2026 results reflected margin expansion, higher adjusted EPS, and share repurchases alongside technology investment, while fiscal 2027 guidance embeds a closed Agile Defense acquisition, no VA MDE incentive contribution across the year, and a sharp step-up in expected free cash flow as delayed collections shift into the new fiscal year; in Q&A, management described the final VA MDE RFP as largely consistent with the draft but with economics moving away from the prior incentive structure toward performance-based volume reallocation.

data.title: Spire downgraded at Jefferies ahead of rate case outcomes
data.description:
Spire (SR) slipped 1.6% in Thursday's trading as Jefferies downgraded the natural gas utility to Hold from Buy with an unchanged $94 price target, saying recent wins leave a more balanced risk/reward while remaining constructive on the company's longer-term earnings profile.

Spire (SR) shares have moved from local distribution company laggard earlier this year to the sector's strongest performer over the past three months, leaving fewer near-term catalysts to drive the stock higher, Jefferies analyst Julien Dumoulin-Smith said.

The company's portfolio has transitioned toward a cleaner regulated gas utility mix, with  Tennessee providing a constructive growth jurisdiction and Missouri Gas adding contracted pipeline earnings, Dumoulin-Smith said, forecasting a 7.3% FY 2028-31 earnings per share compound annual growth rate, modestly above the 7% guidance midpoint, with the Missouri recovery supporting the FY 2028 step-up.

The Missouri rate case remains the largest FY 2028 swing factor, according to the analyst, who modeled $111M, or ~65%, of the $171M of Spire's (SR) net new request, supporting a 9.8% earned return on equity.

Following the stock's recent outperformance, the analyst said he awaits greater visibility on Missouri's execution and balance sheet improvement before turning more positive.

data.title: Meta sets $300 price on pocket-sized Muse Charm AI device: report
data.description:
Meta Platforms (META) has set a $300 price on its upcoming AI gadget, Muse Charm, according to The Information.

To drive up consumer interests, Meta is also offering a free, 12-month 5G data plan from Verizon (VZ), the report said. Meta pushed back the release of its smartwatch until 2027 to get the Muse Charm on the market before Christmas. Earlier this year, Meta set a goal of selling 10M wearable devices during the second half of 2026 as it pushes into a market led by Apple (AAPL).

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg introduced Charm during its Connect event in September. Roughly the size of an Apple AirPods case, Charm features an approximately 2-inch OLED touchscreen and built-in 5G connectivity. It expects to begin shipping the devices by early December.

Zuckerberg said Charm brings the company's Muse personal AI agent into a portable device that can be carried on a keychain, in a pocket, or with a wrist strap.

"We pack the whole Muse experience, including the whole real-time voice and avatar stack, into something that fits on a keychain and is always available to talk to," he said.

The device includes speakers, microphones, front- and rear-facing cameras, a USB-C port, and a customizable virtual Muse character, including options for its appearance and voice. Charm is designed as a dedicated interface for Muse rather than a smartphone replacement. It can connect to Muse over 5G when Wi-Fi is unavailable and is paired and synchronized through the Muse app on an iPhone or Android device. It also supports music and video playback but does not offer phone or video calling. Charm devices can interact with each other as well.

In addition to the Charm and the upcoming smartwatch, Meta is also working on an AI pendant.

data.title: ServiceNow created AI tool to go after Salesforce customers: report
data.description:
• ServiceNow (NOW) created an artificial intelligence tool that automates where a customer's data lives, effectively going after Salesforce's (CRM) business, The Information reported, citing an interview with ServiceNow executive Paul Fipps.
  • Fipps, who is ServiceNow’s president of global customer operations, told the news outlet that the process of finding where data lives on various systems in an effort to extract and move onto ServiceNow's software was previously done manually. 
  • Salesforce shares were down 2.8% in late afternoon trading on Thursday, while ServiceNow fell 1.6%. Technology stocks dropped sharply on Thursday following the initial public offering of AI frontier lab Anthropic (ANT).

data.title: Hedge funds trim AMD stakes in Q3 as two exit entirely
data.description:
Hedge fund activity in Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) was tilted toward selling in the third quarter, even as the stock outperformed the broader market.

Out of the six hedge fund-reported AMD positions, two exited their positions entirely, two reduced their holdings, one increased its stake, and one maintained its position, according to the latest 13F filings.

AMD shares gained 13.10% during the third quarter, outperforming the S&P 500's (SP500) 2.25% advance.

Among the notable sellers, Duquesne Family Office, led by Stanley Druckenmiller, exited its 73K AMD share position, while Appaloosa Management, led by David Tepper, sold its entire 198K-share stake during the quarter.

Other investors significantly reduced their exposure. Soros Capital, led by Robert Soros, cut its AMD holdings by approximately 98.5%, from 52K shares to just 798 shares.

Discovery Capital, led by Rob Citrone, reduced its position by 62.5%, bringing its holdings down to 3K shares from 8K.

Glenview Capital, led by Larry Robbins and Mark Horowitz, was the only fund among the five that traded AMD to increase its stake. The firm raised its holdings by approximately 31.2%, to 391K shares from 298K.

Tiger Global, meanwhile, kept its 675K-share AMD position unchanged during the quarter.

data.title: Gemini gains ability to navigate Mac apps for users
data.description:
Google (GOOG) has rolled out a new capability for its Gemini AI assistant that allows it to operate Mac computers and carry out tasks across applications, adding to the growing competition in the AI agent market.

Dubbed "computer use," the feature enables Gemini to interact with software by clicking through menus, entering text, and completing online forms. Google (GOOG) said users could employ it for tasks such as adjusting batches of photographs in design applications or sorting clothing images saved on their computers for resale listings.

The service is currently available to US users of the Mac Gemini application who subscribe to Google (GOOG) AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra plans.

Gemini runs in a separate background window, allowing users to continue using their primary screen. They can limit the applications accessible to the assistant, observe its activity, interrupt operations, and authorize important actions before they are carried out.

The move puts Google (GOOG) alongside OpenAI’s (OPENAI) ChatGPT and Meta (META) Platforms’ Muse, which already offer similar computer-interaction capabilities on Mac software.

The expansion of such tools could increase pressure on Apple (AAPL) to strengthen Siri’s ability to work with third-party applications. Apple (AAPL) has also flagged privacy concerns linked to AI software accessing extensive user data and promised additional safeguards for Mac computers.

data.title: Bloom Energy upgraded at BMO as order momentum builds
data.description:
Bloom Energy (BE) wobbled between small gains and losses in Thursday's trading as BMO Capital upgraded shares to Outperform from Market Perform with a $230 price target, following recent meetings with CFO Simon Edwards and investor relations VP Michael Tierney.

BMO analyst Ameet Thakkar said he had previously been among the more cautious voices on the company, questioning large-scale proof-of-concept, the durability of a higher-cost generation solution once turbine and grid availability improve, and reliance on U.S. data center demand.

"Those debates remain, but the setup has changed," Thakkar wrote, noting the shares have pulled back and large projects including Nebius are increasingly providing the execution evidence the analyst had sought, and he now believes the risk-reward for investors is more attractive.

Thakkar said BMO's meetings with the Bloom (BE) executives "provided greater comfort around contractual protections, milestone-based customer payments, project finance structures, manufacturing scalability, and continued cost-down opportunities."

The analyst also cited encouraging signs that Bloom (BE) is increasingly being considered during initial power-system design decisions, rather than solely as a workaround for unavailable conventional power.

data.title: Netflix is considered the frontrunner to win the 2030 World Cup media rights
data.description:
The deadline passed on Thursday for the U.S. media rights to the 2030 and 2034 FIFA Men’s World Cups. Notably, several major legacy media and tech giants have reportedly opted out of the bidding. 

While it was no surprise that Skydance (SKYD) bowed out to focus on debt reduction and cost-cutting following its massive merger with Warner Bros. Discovery, the exit of Disney/ESPN (DIS) and Apple (AAPL) from the World Cup bidding was not clear until today. That means the frontrunner to win the bidding rights is Netflix (NFLX) which already secured U.S. rights for the 2027 and 2031 Women's World Cups. Other tech platforms expected to submit bids include Amazon (AMZN) and Google's (GOOG) (GOOGL) YouTube. Fox (FOX) (FOXA) is also expected to bid, while NBCUniversal (Telemundo/Peacock) was reported by CNBC to be debating its final decision right up to the deadline. 

Notably, for the 2030 and 2034 Men’s World Cups, FIFA is no longer selling U.S. Spanish-language rights separately. Instead, it is looking to bundle English- and Spanish-language rights together into a single package.
